alternative_explanations: A finite Mealy-machine table may explain all learned transitions and transfer more cheaply; sparse scheduling may only be ordinary discrete-event simulation, while majority repair may be hand-designed redundancy rather than self-organization.
confounds: The raw local transition atoms are exhaustively demonstrated for four descriptors, graphs are synthetic three-node active cycles inside K=8/32 substrates, and the one-hidden-layer indicator rule can behave as a neural lookup. All candidates are charged the same raw K-node topology/state input; no language or successor-to-LLM claim is permitted.
falsification_criteria: Make HYP-0006 dormant if learned sparse NCA is below 0.95 in any cell, fails one-bit repair or retention, is behaviorally equivalent to the exact finite-state control while losing registered workload or state, or obtains its advantage only by omitting raw topology/state construction or irregular memory charges.

outcome_policy.negative: Failure of learned recurrent transfer, repair, or stable scaling rejects this implementation and makes HYP-0006 dormant without tuning the frozen cohort.
outcome_policy.null: Matched transfer and repair with exact finite-state dominance or neural-table equivalence makes the current HYP-0006 route dormant while retaining sparse event execution as a generic control.
outcome_policy.positive: Only a learned sparse rule that is accurate, regeneration-capable, structurally distinct from exact finite-state propagation and non-dominated under full workload justifies a broader screen.

predicted_outcome: The stateless BFS and random controls should fail because branch choices depend on persistent state and revisits. Exact finite-state, dense learned NCA, sparse learned NCA and oracle should reach perfect cold, warm, held-out-composition and one-bit-repair accuracy. Sparse learned execution should use far fewer rule evaluations than the dense sweep at K=32, but the exact finite-state table is predicted to match its behavior with lower state, update and R16 workload, yielding a classical-automaton null.
promotion_criteria: Quick cannot promote. Advance only if learned sparse NCA has at least 0.95 cold, warm, held-out-composition and repair accuracy in every cell, differs behaviorally from the exact finite-state table, lies on a full-system Pareto frontier against exact and oracle controls, transfers across K and cyclic revisit depth, and passes frozen integrity without tuning.
research_question: Can a learned sparse neural cellular rule transfer nonlinear recurrent state switching and one-bit regeneration across held-out cyclic graph compositions while remaining non-dominated by exact finite-state propagation after full input, memory, fit, update and workload accounting?
title: Nonlinear recurrent local-state transfer on cyclic graphs
